explanation: Try each possible text start unless ^ anchors the pattern. Recursively match one ordinary character, or enumerate all compatible repetition lengths for a starred token; a trailing $ requires the remaining text to be empty.
timeComplexity: O((p+1)(n+1)): at most one evaluation of each pattern/text offset pair, with constant work and at most two transitions per state.
spaceComplexity: O((p+1)(n+1)) cached states plus O(p+n+1) recursion frames; every recursive step advances a pattern or text offset.

correctness: At each pattern suffix, an ordinary token must match exactly the next text character. A starred token can consume any prefix consisting only of compatible characters, including length zero; the loop and final zero-length branch cover exactly those choices. Exhausting the pattern succeeds unless its trailing end anchor still requires more text to be consumed. Trying all starts implements substring matching.
walkthrough: For ^ab*c$ on abbbc, the anchor fixes start 0 and a consumes the first character. The b* branch tries one b (c then fails), two b characters (c still fails), then three b characters. The remaining c matches and $ sees empty text, so return true.
edgeCases: An unanchored pattern may match an empty substring.
^ anchors only the beginning and a trailing $ anchors the end.
A starred token may consume zero characters.
Dot matches one character, not an arbitrary-length substring.
